threads.title: Show HN: SoundEtch, an open source podcast/media editor for the desktop browser
topics: a personal archive read by machine
threads.text:
I've been working on this project for a few years, and thinking about it for a few more years. Ever since the pandemic when I did my entire job on a little Chromebook with browser-based tools; why not make an Audacity for the browser?
Well, it turned out there were already a few "Audacities for the Browser" like https://audiomass.co/ (posted here a couple times already), https://naomiaro.com/waveform-playlist/, and a literal Audacity compiled to WebAssembly https://wavacity.com/. SoundEtch is kind of a beefed up version of those.
I made it with podcasters and other spoken-word creators in mind, rather than musicians, since there are a number of browser DAWs already e.g. OpenDAW.
Everything is streamed to and from disk (OPFS), with an optional cloud backup. You can close or crash the browser tab, even in the middle of recording, and your data is still there when you open it back up. This also means you can load huge files; my parents' desktop with 8gb RAM handled this 5 hour stereo mp3 I found on archive https://archive.org/details/2023-09-08/2023-09-10.mp3.
There's a transcription-based editing tool like you get with Riverside and Descript. Mine uses IBM's Granite Turbo model, plus some Codex/Claude tweaking to get word-level timestamps. The result is, to my knowledge, much faster and more accurate than any other browser/local ASR out there. It has a few quirks, though, like only emitting lower-case letters and spaces.
I also added a WebRTC meeting room with up to 4 guests. I […]

threads.title: Ask HN: How to validate my idea/MVP?
threads.text:
I'm currently building Apartment Archive, which is an online interior design business focused on making personalized interior design and space planning more accessible.
I've spent quite a bit of time building out the website and figuring out the service itself. I'm at a point where I'd like to validate the idea, get a better sense of product-market fit and see whether there's enough demand before building much further.
I've been reading about smoke testing (a facade MVP or even just a landing page with a call to action to gauge interest), but I'm more curious about how people have actually gone about doing this in practice. I'm wondering how to go about this when starting without an existing audience.
Where did you find your first potential customers? Were there any communities, groups, or specific approaches that worked particularly well for you?
I'm also trying to get some clarity around how people distinguished between someone thinking their idea was interesting and someone actually being willing to pay for it. I've conducted some user testing which was helpful in getting a better understanding of what people want and don't want, but I'd like to find a way to gauge whether people would actually pay for the service.
Would appreciate hearing what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently if you were starting from scratch.
Thank you in advance for your help! I appreciate you taking the time to read my post.

threads.title: Show HN: DragDropMath – Learn math by feel
threads.text:
Hi HN!
I am a professional physicist and I shuffle symbols in equations and mathematical expressions all day long. During my PhD (almost 20 years ago) I noticed that it is as if the symbols have their own 'physics', which makes the wrong moves impossible and the right ones obvious.
So I created DragDropMath, where you can learn how to simplify mathematical expressions and how to solve equations by dragging symbols around, and only correct moves are allowed, so you get to feel what's right without experiencing (and so learning) wrong moves.
I always wanted to make this, but life got in the way. Then a few weeks ago I saw declarative dragging (https://declarative-dragging.github.io/) on the front page of HN and the spark came back!
It took quite a few rounds to get the feel right, but I think it's close to what happens in my mind when I mentally manipulate these expressions.
A few more points:
- There are no ads, no trackers, no accounts (it's a static website and progress is saved in the browser cache).
- Teachers can create their own problem sets, encoded in the link.
- I plan to add more chapters (trigonometry, complex numbers, some calculus) but I first need to figure out the 'right' mode of interaction.
- I just started working on the experience from mobile, so there may still be some rough edges there
I'm curious to know what you think, if you have suggestions for content, if you spot anything that I should fix, if you have feature requests! Thank you in advance

threads.title: Show HN: Yioop 10 – a PHP search engine that runs groups, wikis, Git and mail
threads.text:
Yioop is an open source (GPLv3) search engine written in PHP that I have been working on since 2009. Version 10 is now out.
Yioop comes with a crawler which can be used on the open web or on a list of sites you choose. It can also index Wikipedia XML dumps, arc and warc archives, Open Directory RDF, and dumps of email or databases, and several crawls can be mixed into one set of results. A media updater re-indexes RSS and Atom feeds every hour, so news makes it into the results.
Besides search, Yioop can be used to run discussion groups, blogs and wikis. Each group has a wiki for pages, slide presentations and spreadsheets, and the wiki can be used to build whole web sites.
Some of what is new in version 10:
- Yioop can run on its own Pure PHP web server, with HTTPS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support, and has its own web configurable PHP mail server and client.
- Users can make voice and video calls from their messages.
- Common audio and video formats are decoded and encoded in Yioop's own PHP code.
- A wiki page can hold a git repository that people clone and push to over HTTP, with an issue tracker beside it.
- Yioop is available in 25 languages, and a faster tokenizer handles text in each of them, including Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
Yioop's stemmers, summarizers and other language tools can also be used in other projects through Composer.
Demo: https://www.yioop.com/
Project page: https://www.seekquarry.com/
